Hi Maya — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we can move to pricing/contract: 

1) Summary of commercial paths we discussed:
- PO (standard vendor PO / net terms): typical enterprise flow. If procurement can accept a vendor PO we can take that route and Redwood Finance will generate net30 terms once vendor onboarding is complete.
- Card / Marketplace purchase: purchase via AWS Marketplace (or other CSP marketplaces) to avoid vendor PO; immediate provisioning and standard marketplace billing.
- Prepay / committed credit: customer prepays for committed usage (invoice up front) in exchange for committed discounts and invoice-based delivery. Useful where PO is not allowed.

2) Edge cases you mentioned we should track:
- If your policy disallows vendor-issued POs for new SaaS vendors, Marketplace or prepay are the primary options.
- First-year onboarding/prepay thresholds (if required) — we can accommodate tiered prepay commitments or a pilot prepay.

3) Ask from our side / next steps:
- Can you confirm whether Ava Retail can/does purchase via AWS Marketplace? If yes, we can produce a Marketplace SKU and quick order form.
- If Marketplace is not an option, can you share the exact prepay / spend threshold your team requires for new vendors? (e.g., minimum $Xk).
- Please share the procurement contact and any vendor policy docs we should follow.

Attaching: Redwood-SOW-template.pdf and procurement-qr-sheet.xlsx for your procurement team to review.

I'll loop in Ben (Sales Ops) and Lauren (Finance) to help with exception paths if PO isn't viable. If you prefer, we can get you a draft order form or DocuSign for signature once we confirm market/place/prepay path.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Hi Rishi — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- Ava Retail policy: our vendor onboarding team is not approving standard vendor POs for new smaller SaaS vendors this year unless the vendor is already in our master vendor list. New vendors are required to either (a) transact via AWS Marketplace, (b) provide an upfront prepay for the first 12 months, or (c) go through an exception approval which usually takes >4 weeks.
- Prepay: Finance has flagged a practical minimum prepay threshold of ~$50k for initial onboarding. Anything below that is typically routed to exception which is slow.

We do prefer Marketplace purchases where possible. Can Redwood confirm if you have (or can create) a Marketplace listing / SKU? If not, can you provide an invoice/purchase order that shows the prepay option and order amounts?

I've attached our vendor policy snapshot (avarail-vendor-policy.pdf) for your finance team.

Thanks —
Maya Singh
Procurement Lead, Ava Retail
maya@avaretail.com
